lines.text: Clock's stopped. Eleven minutes past six this morning. My father wound that clock, and his father, and it's never once stopped.
There's rime on the case, and in the works too, I don't doubt. I can't get a hand in there without breaking something.
They say you got Silas's press going.
They say you've a way with cold.
It's in the house. Door's open. Mind the stairs, they've got opinions.
Still eleven past six in there. Feels later.
The tall clock stands with rime across its face, stopped at eleven minutes past six.
Easy, now. Nobody's asking you to hurry.
Somewhere inside, a small wet tick. Then another. Then, very late and not at all sorry, it strikes.
There. You've only lost a morning. There's worse to lose.
Tick. Tick. Hours behind the church, and not troubled by it.
I know. I heard it strike, clear across the Green.
It's wrong, of course. Lost a whole morning. I'll leave it wrong a day or two. Seems rude to correct it.
Here. Spare key to the case, and a drop of tonic. You look as if you've been up since six yourself.
